independent_numerics.acceleration_reasoning: For parallel finite force, dp/dv=m0*gamma^3 and a_parallel=F_parallel/(m0*gamma^3); transverse a=F_transverse/(m0*gamma). Both tend to0 for bounded force and fixed positive m0 as v->c. Force changes momentum, not a velocity-independent relativistic scalar inertia.
independent_numerics.circular_force_reasoning: For uniform circular motion at fixed speed and radius, |dp/dt|=gamma*m0*v^2/r; relative to classical m0*v^2/r the ratio is gamma.
independent_numerics.proton_comparison_reasoning: At gamma approximately2000, gamma*m_e exceeds m_p because m_p/m_e is approximately1836; compare relativistic electron mass to proton rest mass, not invariant electron mass to invariant proton mass.

findings.title: Distinguish finite-interval average force from instantaneous force

evidence_quotes.zh: 在连续时间的写法中，这就是 d(mv)/dt=F，各量的方向按向量处理。
evidence_quotes.en: In continuous time, this is d(mv)/dt=F, with directions understood as vectors.

findings.problem: The displayed source equation uses a finite difference Delta p/Delta t, but both modern paragraphs identify it with an instantaneous derivative without specifying Delta t approaching zero. Neither locale explains that for a finite interval the right side must mean the average net force, except when the force is constant. Continuous motion alone does not make these quantities equal. The earlier constant-force example does not constrain the later general law or circular-motion example, whose force direction changes.
independent_reasoning: The instantaneous momentum law is F(t)=dp(t)/dt.
Integrating over [t1,t2] gives Delta p/Delta t=(1/Delta t)*integral(F(t) dt), the interval-average force.
The finite quotient tends to instantaneous force as Delta t tends to zero where the derivative exists.
A one-component counterexample p(t)=t^2 on [0,1] has interval quotient1, while F(1)=2 and F(0)=0. It is continuous and differentiable, so 'in continuous time' alone is insufficient.

smallest_repair.zh: Replace the quoted sentence with wording that states: for a finite time interval F means the interval-average resultant force (and is simply the force if constant); as the interval tends to zero, the equation becomes the instantaneous vector law d(mv)/dt=F.
smallest_repair.en: Replace the quoted sentence with wording that states: over a finite time interval F denotes the average net force (equal to the force when constant); as the interval tends to zero, the equation becomes the instantaneous vector law d(mv)/dt=F.
